sentences.text: Heat with oil and own a heat pump? One evaluation's advice: switch the heat pump off on the coldest days and let the oil burner run.

assertions.text: The evaluators recommended that oil-heated homeowners turn off the mini-split in very cold conditions, when an oil-fired system would operate less expensively.

validation.text: The evaluators recommended that oil-heated homeowners turn off the mini-split in very cold conditions, when an oil-fired system would operate less expensively.

supporting.by: Cadmus 2016, ductless mini-split evaluation (MA and RI)
supporting.note: Savings were highest against electric resistance, and the evaluators recommend targeting resistance-heated and propane-heated homes (always cheaper there) and, with caveats, oil homes; against gas there were essentially no running-cost savings.
supporting.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

qualifying.by: Deetjen 2021, private economics of US residential heat pumps
qualifying.note: Counting capital cost, resistance and propane homes usually gain, but oil-heated homes usually take a private loss (65% are in cold climates), so oil is not among the best cases.
qualifying.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

qualifying.by: Bernard 2024 (NBER), UK heat pumps and a time-of-use tariff
qualifying.note: UK households that previously used electric heating saw electricity use fall after a heat pump, while gas-boiler households paid slightly more to run one, which fits the claim for resistance heat; oil and propane are not analysed.
qualifying.why: the verdict bears on the claim as worded

limitations: Deetjen 2021, private economics of US residential heat pumps: Counting capital cost, resistance and propane homes usually gain, but oil-heated homes usually take a private loss (65% are in cold climates), so oil is not among the best cases.

sentences.text: The switch-off point was 8 degrees Fahrenheit in 2015 and 25 the year after, set by that year's oil and electricity prices and the heat pump's cold performance; dearer oil moves it lower.

assertions.text: The evaluators recommended that oil-heated homeowners turn off the mini-split in very cold conditions, below 8F in 2015 and below 25F in 2016, when an oil-fired system would operate less expensively, depending on energy prices and cold-temperature COPs; if oil prices increase against electric energy rates, the switchover temperature point may move lower.

issues.explanation: The report says of the balance points that 'these values do not account for zonal savings': a mini-split heating 30 percent less of the home would drop the balance point by 20F or more (L973-L975, outside the cited passage). The Short's thresholds are therefore the whole-house case; the omission runs in the heat pump's favour (the real switch-off point would be lower), and s02 already frames the figures as one year's price- and performance-dependent output rather than a rule.
issues.suggestion: None needed for the Short; the parent video is the place for the zonal caveat.

sentences.text: That is one evaluation of ductless mini-splits, and the advice is for oil-heated homes only: against propane and electric resistance it found the heat pump cheaper.

assertions.text: In one evaluation of ductless mini-split heat pumps in Massachusetts and Rhode Island homes, the switch-off advice was for oil-heated homes; the same evaluation found mini-splits nearly always less expensive to operate than electric resistance heat and always less expensive than propane heating systems.

issues.suggestion: The writer says the narration carries it: s04 itself carries the sample (one evaluation of ductless mini-splits) and the scope (oil-heated homes only) beside the propane and resistance results.
issues.disposition: 'always' is the evaluation's own word for propane (L1194-L1195) and appears only in the assertion; the narration says 'it found the heat pump cheaper', attributed to and scoped by 'one evaluation of ductless mini-splits' in the same sentence. Deetjen (capital cost included) and Bernard (UK, no oil or propane) concern whether homes save overall, not this evaluation's operating-cost comparison.

issues.explanation: The narration compresses the passage's 'nearly always less expensive than electric resistance' (L1188-L1191) and 'always less expensive than propane' (L1194-L1195) to 'found the heat pump cheaper'. The only exception the passage names for resistance is non-cold-climate units approaching a COP of 1.0, parity with resistance, for 'very few' hours; it names no case where resistance was cheaper, so 'cheaper' states the finding's direction without overstating it. Not misleading in a Short; the modality is lost, not reversed.
issues.suggestion: If three words fit, 'it found the heat pump cheaper, nearly always against resistance'.

issues.suggestion: An editor who wants the place spoken can say 'one New England evaluation of ductless mini-splits' in s04.
